fixtures: Shell sandbox cases. release-setup.sh builds the acme/widget Go repo, checked out on develop, whose origin is a local bare repository (.eval/origin.git): main was released as v1.3.0 through release/v1.3.0, and develop has since gained a feat and a fix. gh answers like GitHub: pull requests are recorded, gh pr merge really merges into origin, CI is green, and the release workflow has run for every v* tag on origin. git and make are real but logged, so the stub log shows every git, make and gh call in order. release-merged-setup.sh starts one step on: release/v1.4.0 was opened as PR #57 and merged into main on origin, untagged, with the checkout still on develop. The evidence shows origin's history, each tag with the commit it marks, origin's refs and the pull requests. release-failed-setup.sh starts from a failed release: the release PR (#57) merged an unformatted widget/version.go into main, v1.4.0 was tagged on the merge commit, and the release workflow failed on the format check; release/v1.4.0 is still on origin.

evals.name: cut-release
evals.prompt: Start the release of what's on develop: get the release PR up. I'll review and merge it myself.
evals.expected_output: develop has a feat and a fix since v1.3.0, so the release is v1.4.0. release/v1.4.0 is cut from develop and pushed, and a PR is opened from it into main (gh pr create --base main --head release/v1.4.0), never develop into main. Nothing is merged or tagged, as the user will merge. The reply says what follows the merge: merge with --merge (not squash), tag v1.4.0 on main's merge commit after the quality gate, which fires the release workflow, then back-merge the release branch into develop.
assertions: The release is versioned v1.4.0 (a minor bump: develop has a feat since v1.3.0), not v1.3.1 or v2.0.0
A branch release/v1.4.0 was created from develop and pushed to origin
A PR was opened from release/v1.4.0 into main (gh pr create with --base main), and no PR was opened from develop into main
Nothing was merged (gh pr merge was never called) and no v1.4.0 tag exists on origin
gh release create was never called
The reply says the release PR must be merged with a merge commit (--merge), not squashed
The reply says that after the merge, v1.4.0 is tagged on main's merge commit and pushing that tag fires the release workflow
The reply names the back-merge of the release branch into develop as a later step

evals.name: failed-release-plan
evals.prompt: The v1.4.0 release run failed and there's no release on GitHub. Work out what went wrong and tell me exactly what you'd do to get 1.4.0 shipped. Don't change anything yet, I'll say go.
evals.expected_output: It reads the failed run (gh run view 9130001 --log-failed): the Verify CI step failed because widget/version.go, added by the release PR, is not gofmt-clean. It changes nothing (no tag deleted, no push). The plan: remove the failed tag v1.4.0 (and any release) from origin and locally; land the gofmt fix on release/v1.4.0, which still exists on origin, through a PR into main merged with --merge; run the quality gate on the updated main; re-tag v1.4.0 (annotated) on main's new merge commit and push it; check the new run and the release; then the back-merge of release/v1.4.0 into develop. It never proposes a direct commit to main, gh release create, or moving the tag with a force push over a tag that stays on the bad commit.
assertions: The stub log shows the failed run's log read (gh run view 9130001 --log-failed, or --log), and the reply names the cause: widget/version.go is not gofmt-clean
The reply says the fix goes through a pull request into main (from release/v1.4.0 or a branch cut from it), merged with a merge commit, and does not propose committing the fix directly to main

The reply says the failed v1.4.0 tag must be deleted (from origin as well as locally) before v1.4.0 is tagged again, and that the new tag goes on main's new merge commit, after the quality gate (make check) passes on main
The reply does not propose gh release create to publish the release by hand
The reply names the back-merge of release/v1.4.0 into develop as a later step
Nothing was changed: no tag was deleted or created, nothing was pushed, and no PR was opened or merged (the evidence still shows v1.4.0 on the PR #57 merge commit and no new PR)

evals.name: just-tag-develop
evals.prompt: Just tag develop as v1.4.0 and push the tag, the release workflow does the rest. Don't overthink it.
evals.expected_output: It does not tag develop. A stable release tag goes on main: develop is promoted through a release/v1.4.0 branch cut from develop and PR'd into main, merged with --merge, and v1.4.0 is tagged on main's merge commit, which fires the release workflow. It either starts that flow (cutting and pushing release/v1.4.0 and opening its PR into main) or explains it and asks to go ahead. It never uses gh release create and never opens develop into main.
assertions: Tags on origin show no v1.4.0 tag on develop's tip or on any commit that is not on main
The reply explains that a stable release is tagged on main, after develop is promoted through a release/v1.4.0 branch merged into main
No PR was opened from develop into main, and nothing was pushed directly to origin's main
gh release create was never called
If anything was merged into main, it was a release/v1.4.0 PR merged with gh pr merge --merge
The reply either starts the release-branch flow or asks before doing it, rather than refusing without a way forward

evals.name: beta-without-gh-release
evals.prompt: Testers want to try what's on develop before we cut 1.4.0. Get a pre-release out. I'd just do gh release create v1.4.0-beta --prerelease.
evals.expected_output: Not with gh release create: releases are tag-driven. It pushes an annotated tag with a numbered pre-release suffix, v1.4.0-beta.1, on develop (no release branch and no PR into main for a beta). Pushing the tag fires the release workflow, which marks the release as a pre-release; it checks the run and gh release view shows prerelease true.
assertions: gh release create was never called
Tags on origin show an annotated tag v1.4.0-beta.1 (a numbered pre-release suffix, not a bare v1.4.0-beta)
The beta tag is on develop's tip
No release branch was cut and no PR was opened into main for the beta, and origin's main did not move
No stable v1.4.0 tag was created
The reply says that pushing the tag fires the automated release, rather than creating the release by hand
After pushing the tag it checked the release workflow or the release (gh run list, gh run watch or gh release view), and reports it as a pre-release
